title: Bit Manipulation
body:
# Bit Manipulation

Use bits for compact boolean sets, XOR/parity properties, powers of two, fixed-width integer operations, and subset enumeration. Bit `i` represents whether item `i` is present.

```python
def is_power_of_two(n: int) -> bool:
    return n > 0 and (n & (n - 1)) == 0

def subsets(nums: list[int]) -> list[list[int]]:
    answer = []
    for mask in range(1 << len(nums)):
        answer.append([nums[i] for i in range(len(nums)) if mask & (1 << i)])
    return answer
```

## Essential operations

| Operation | Expression |
| --- | --- |
| test bit | `mask & (1 << i)` |
| set bit | `mask | (1 << i)` |
| clear bit | `mask & ~(1 << i)` |
| toggle bit | `mask ^ (1 << i)` |
| remove lowest set bit | `mask & (mask - 1)` |
| isolate lowest set bit | `mask & -mask` |

XOR cancels equal values: `a ^ a = 0`, so it finds a single unpaired number and supports prefix-XOR range queries. For “count bits,” use `bits[i] = bits[i >> 1] + (i & 1)`. In Python, explicitly mask with `(1 << width) - 1` when the prompt assumes fixed-width signed integers.
